newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wage demands too high -- BDA employers leader.
newsitem.headline: German wage demands too high -- BDA employers leader.

text.p: Dieter Hundt, head of the BDA German employers association, said current wage agreements in Germany were still damaging its ability to compete in the global economy.

Speaking at a two-day employment conference organised by trade unions in Berlin, he said that the increase in international trade was increasing the pressure for a reform of Germany's collective wage bargaining system.
"Globalisation was not a German investment...But there need be no losers within a growing world economy," Hundt said during a panel discussion at the conference.

Recent wage agreements, such as those signed for the three million-plus workers in the German metal and engineering sector, have been much lower than in recent years and have mostly been around the rate of inflation.
But Hundt insisted that job creation in Germany was being held back by excessive labour costs.

He urged trade unions to tone down future wage demands still further and called on the government to support innovation and new product development or risk being "run over" in the face of economic globalisation.
